\[p_s(n) = a_n\]for $0 \le n \le 9.$  For example, $p(x) = p_{(0,1,0,0,1,0,1,0,0,0)}(x)$ is the polynomial of degree at most 9 such that $p(0) = p(2) = p(3) = p(5) = p(7) = p(8) = p(9) = 0$ and $p(1) = p(4) = p(6) = 1.$

\[\sum_{s \in S} p_s(10).\]

The sum of all such polynomials evaluated at \( x = 10 \) can be found by considering the sum of all polynomials \( p_s(x) \) first, and then evaluating this sum at \( x = 10 \).

3. **Constant Polynomial**: Since \( P(n) = 512 \) for all \( n \) from 0 to 9, \( P(x) \) must be a constant polynomial. This is because a polynomial of degree at most 9 that takes the same value at 10 distinct points must be constant.

4. **Evaluation at 10**: The constant value of the polynomial \( P(x) \) is 512, so \( P(10) = 512 \).
